depts.n: Home altars, shrines and sacred images

k.d: Cabinet, shelf or box shrine kept in a home or room to hold sacred images, name tablets or talismans; style (modern, karaki, gold-leaf), wall-hung installation and compact or mini size are attributes.
Rope hung to mark a sacred space or object in a rite (shimenawa a named form); a seasonal festival decoration such as the kadomatsu is B4.
Wand of zigzag paper or metal-foil streamers set at a shrine or household altar as the sign of the kami's presence (gohei, kinpei named forms).
Sacred picture painted on a rigid panel, framed or mounted to stand or hang (icon a named form).
Sacred picture painted or printed on cloth or paper and mounted as a hanging scroll or rolled for hanging (thangka, kakejiku honzon scroll, pata).
Large sacred picture or carved screen made to stand behind or above an altar, old-master altarpieces included (K-108).
Sculpted figure of a holy person, deity or saint made to be venerated; the figure is an iconography tag, not a kind.
Cross, with or without a figure on it, made to stand, hang or be held in veneration (crucifix a named form).
Boxed or composed set of figures and a stable showing the birth of Jesus, sold and compared as one set (K-1).
Small model of a stupa or chorten made to stand on an altar as a sacred focus, filled with relics or mantras or not (chorten a named form).
Body part or belonging of a holy person, or a thing touched to one, kept for veneration; `relic_class` (first, second, third) is a classification attribute.
Case or container made to hold and show a relic.

b.m: form and style for the rite
b.w: Standing, Tau, St Benedict crosses and the like.
Origin as a tag, never a level.

k.d: String or loop of beads, knots or counters made to count prayers, with or without a cross, counter, tassel or guru bead (rosary, chaplet, tasbih, mala, juzu named forms); a necklace of the same beads made as jewellery is A3 (K-111).

Rug or mat made to kneel, stand or prostrate on in prayer; `padding`, `non_slip_base` and `surface_fabric` are attributes, travel and children's are setting and user tags; a meditation cushion or mat is B2 (K-113).
Cylinder holding written prayers, turned by hand, wind or water.
Cloth flag printed with prayers or sacred images, hung to be blown by the wind.

s.n: Medals, cards, holy water and charms

k.d: Loose medal of a saint or sacred subject made for devotion; one made with a chain or bail to be worn is A3, one struck to commemorate or reward F3 (K-107).
Printed card with a sacred image or prayer, kept or carried for devotion (K-112).
Small basin for holy water, hung or stood by a door or in a room.
Bottle or flask made to hold blessed water.
Small charm carried, not worn as jewellery, for luck, protection or a named blessing (omamori, carried evil-eye charm); worn A3, issued for money F3 (K-117).

b.m: right for the use and tradition
b.v: 108 beads or shorter; juzu by sect and wearer

b.w: Bodhi seed, sandalwood, stone; perfectly uniform colour may mean treated or imitation.
Cord, knots, drill holes, guru bead.

depts.n: Ritual vessels, implements and sacred scrolls

k.d: Cup or goblet made to hold wine or another drink used in a rite (chalice, kiddush cup named forms).
Display vessel with a window or frame, made to show a consecrated host.
Plate or tray made to hold the symbolic foods of a rite; the food itself is not F4.
Lidded cup, bowl or box made to hold consecrated or unconsecrated hosts (ciborium, pyx, host box named forms).
Cup, usually two-handled, made to pour water over the hands in ritual washing (netilat yadayim cup a named form).
Small box or tower made to hold fragrant spices smelled in the Havdalah rite (besamim box a named form).
Sprinkler for holy water.
Slim rod ending in a pointing hand, held to follow the text when reading a scroll aloud.
Short sceptre held in the hand in a rite.
Knife or blade made to be held in a rite, not to cut (athame, boline named forms).
Spoon or ladle made to pour or offer water, ghee or a sacrament in a rite (achamani, fire-offering ladle, communion spoon named forms).
Case made to hold a doorpost scroll and be fixed to a doorpost; material is an attribute.
Handwritten parchment strip of sacred text made to be put in a case and fixed to a doorpost; `script_style` and size class (to fit the case) are attributes, the kosher grade a registry row only.
Pair of small boxes holding handwritten sacred passages, with straps, made to be strapped to the arm and head in prayer.
Handwritten scroll of the Five Books on parchment, made to be read in the rite; a printed Torah or Bible is F1 (K-112).
Horn made to be blown in a rite.
Bell held by a handle and rung in a rite or service (altar bell, sanctus bell, ghanta named forms).
Bowl-shaped bell that rests on a cushion or stand and is struck with a striker, made for a rite (rin; singing bowl only when made for a rite, otherwise E3, K-110).
Hollow wooden block struck to keep rhythm in chanting (mokugyo a named form).
Small two-headed hand drum, often hourglass-shaped with pellets on cords, rattled or struck in a rite (damaru a named form); one sold for music is E3.
Pair of small thick cymbals joined by a cord, struck together in a rite (tingsha a named form); ones sold for meditation are E3.

b.w: First: rests on the scribe's reliability and rabbinical certification.

b.m: fit of scroll to case (scroll goods)
fit to scroll, doorway and mounting (mezuzah case)

k.d: Nine-branch lamp or candle holder, eight places for the festival lights and one for the helper light.
Seven-branch lamp or candle holder.
Lamp burning oil or ghee, made for worship (diya, butter-lamp holder named forms).
Lamp kept burning before a sanctuary or altar; electric or LED is a power attribute.
Candle holder made to stand on or by an altar in a rite; an open candle holder for the home is B4 (K-180).
Candle made for a rite or devotion, including altar, votive, procession, Easter, grave, Yahrzeit and memorial candles (K-113); occasion is a tag, wax content and power attributes.
Wreath with candles used to count the weeks before Christmas.

Lantern made to be hung or set out in a rite or as a shrine offering (bon lantern, votive stone tōrō named forms); a garden tōrō or decorative lantern is B4, a lantern made to be carried as a light B3 (K-116, K-180).
Incense made for a rite, in stick, cone, resin or church grade (senko, agarbatti named forms; a smudge bundle made for a named rite, K-115).
Standing or hanging vessel for burning incense (koro, joss-stick pot, dhoop stand named forms; grave incense holders with setting tag grave).
Incense burner hung on chains, to be swung.
Bowl, cup or vase made to hold water, rice, tea, flowers or other offerings (rice vessel, tea cup, altar flower vase; grave flower vases with setting tag grave).
Box, plate or basket made to collect money given as alms, charity or offering in religious practice (church collection box, tzedakah box, saisen box named forms).
Stand or tray made to hold offerings.
78-card deck with major and minor suits, sold for divination; each published deck design is a maker-bound named form under its publisher; a pack sold for card play is E1 (K-109).
Deck of cards with its own set of images and messages, any number of cards, sold for divination.
36-card deck of the Lenormand pattern, sold for divination.
Sphere used for scrying.
Lettered board with a pointer, made for divination; made as a board game it is E1 (K-114).
Set of stones, wood or tiles marked with runes, made for casting.
Coins or sticks made for casting the I Ching.
Weight on a chain or cord, made to be dangled for divination.
Rod, pair of L-rods or forked rod made to be held for dowsing or divination; one sold as a survey or pipe-finding tool goes with tools.
Box that holds a body for burial or cremation; material, steel gauge, shape, sealing and biodegradable are attributes (rental casket a named form).
Container for cremated remains, of any capacity from a keepsake portion to a companion pair (`capacity_class`); not a worn piece of jewellery (F4-O1); pet urns carry a user tag.
m: Forever Yours Cremation Urns for Two
Together Always Cremation Urns for Two

k.d: Container made to release ashes on land, water or from the air.
Outer box or liner made to hold an urn in the ground.
Stone or plaque set on or at a grave (tombstone, tomb slab named forms).
Tablet that stands for a dead person, inscribed with a name, kept at an altar or home (ihai a named form).
Book or folding album made to record the names and death dates of the dead, kept at a household altar (kakocho a named form).
Cloth laid over a coffin (coffin cover a named form).

k.d: Cloth or set of cloths that wrap the body.

k.d: Ornament fitted to the top of a scroll's rollers.

k.d: Plate fixed to a coffin, naming the dead.
Pillow made for the inside of a coffin.
Plaque, appliqué or medallion made to be fixed to an urn.
